images.title: What bi and tri count
images.purpose: Shows a billion as 1000 with 2 more 1000s multiplied on, and a trillion as 1000 with 3 more, so the first part of the name counts them.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. Two rows of 1000 blocks, one above the other, each with its name on the left and its power of 10 on the right.
images.exact_structure: Row 1: the label 'billion' at the left, then one teal (#0072B2) block showing '1000', then a '×', then exactly 2 amber (#E69F00) blocks each showing '1000' joined by a '×'; a small amber (#E69F00) brace under the 2 amber blocks labelled 'bi: 2'; at the right the label '10⁹'. Row 2: the label 'trillion', one teal (#0072B2) block '1000', a '×', then exactly 3 amber (#E69F00) blocks '1000' joined by '×' signs; a brace under the 3 amber blocks labelled 'tri: 3'; at the right '10¹²'. Exactly 7 blocks, 2 braces.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The first part of each name counts the extra 1000s: bi 2, tri 3, quadri 4, quinti 5.
images.description: Shows a billion as 1000 with 2 more 1000s multiplied on, and a trillion as 1000 with 3 more, so the first part of the name counts them.
images.context: 1000 × 1000 × 1000 = 10⁹, and four 1000s multiplied make 10 to the power 12.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the extra 1000s counted makes the meaning of bi and tri visible, which is the whole task.
